evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Viewing sponsors can be implemented as a standalone listing feature without requiring another specific story to be completed first.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Listing user profiles inherently depends on users/accounts existing (registration/account creation).

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Bulk emailing trainers can be delivered as an admin/coordinator function without requiring another specific backlog story as a prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: A map page/asset can be implemented independently of other stories.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Trainer self-editing of training content can be implemented as a standalone capability; it does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: This constraint depends on having a registration process/workflow in place.

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee
evaluations.rationale: Tracking registration status depends on attendees being able to register and having registration records.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: A waitlist inherently depends on an underlying training registration/capacity mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Acceptance of cancellation terms depends on an existing registration/cancellation workflow where such a checkbox can be presented.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: This explicitly depends on a registration/cancellation workflow existing.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: The story explicitly depends on the existence of a schedule feature.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Seeing signed-up trainings depends on the ability to sign up/register for trainings.

evaluations.evidence: view ... attached to their training node that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: Showing attendee information for a training depends on attendees being registered/signed up for that training.

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: An admin view of trainee information per training session depends on trainees registering/signing up and those records existing.

evaluations.evidence: dedicated page for each class ... link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: A class detail page can be implemented independently; the register link can exist even if registration is implemented later.

evaluations.evidence: training options clearly marked ... register now link
evaluations.rationale: A training listing page can be implemented independently; links can be placeholders without requiring another story first.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page ... list of all training offerings
evaluations.rationale: A landing page and listing can be implemented as a standalone content/navigation feature.

evaluations.evidence: link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A link to a list of training options depends on that list/page existing.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: This can be implemented as standalone informational content.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refund capability can be implemented as an admin function without requiring another specific story as a prerequisite (it relies on existing payments but no explicit backlog dependency is stated).

evaluations.evidence: find a link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the sponsorships page (sponsor listing/page) existing.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: This depends on having attendee accounts/registrations and a way to associate attendees with a company/sponsor.

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Paying for sponsorship inherently depends on payment processing capability being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Venue CRUD can be implemented as a standalone administrative feature.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details depends on venues being created/maintained.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: This depends on sessions existing and on sponsor-attendee associations being available.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: A third-step payment page inherently depends on the registration process existing.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors to events/trainings/summits depends on sponsors and those entities existing.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: This depends on sponsors being assigned to events/trainings/summits.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged
evaluations.rationale: Payment processing for individual sponsorship can be implemented as a standalone capability without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Linking attendees to a sponsorship page depends on having attendee accounts/registrations and a sponsorship page/profile to link to.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating a user profile depends on having a user account/profile created via registration.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup can be implemented independently as a standalone form/subscription feature.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Tagging blog posts depends on blog posts existing/being created.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a standalone content creation feature.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog depends on blog posts existing to read.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit depends on summits existing to sponsor.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Registering for a summit depends on summits being defined/listed.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Directions to the summit venue depend on summit venue/location information being defined.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Seeing signed-up summits depends on the ability to register for summits and store those registrations.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: A list of summit attendees depends on summit registration being implemented and having signups.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Entering/listing summit information can be implemented as a standalone content management feature.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing sponsors for a summit depends on sponsors being associated with that summit.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: A summit agenda can be implemented as standalone content for a summit.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Seats remaining depends on summit registration/capacity tracking being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: Summit details depend on summit information being created/listed.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A summits listing can be implemented as a standalone feature (it can exist even before rich summit details are added).

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Sponsorship levels information can be implemented as standalone informational content.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Adding a WYSIWYG editor is a standalone platform capability and does not inherently depend on another story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Linking from job listings to a sponsorship profile depends on both job listings existing and sponsorship profiles existing.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: This can be implemented as standalone informational content and contact details.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Job posting can be implemented as a standalone feature (sponsor eligibility is implied by role but not an inherent dependency on another specific story).

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board depends on job postings existing to display.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location, so that I can populate the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Assigning rooms/time slots to populate the schedule depends on having venues/rooms/locations defined.

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the schedule depends on the schedule being populated/created.

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: A final list of approved sessions depends on sessions being submitted and accepted/approved.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk approving sessions depends on sessions having been submitted and existing in the system.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Marking a session accepted depends on sessions being submitted and existing.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Notifications about evaluation depend on a session submission and evaluation/acceptance process existing.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the ability to submit a session.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing a session depends on a session having been submitted/created.

evaluations.rationale: Registering to speak is tied to submitting a session and depends on session submission capability.

evaluations.evidence: As a authenticateduser, I want to submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session as an authenticated user depends on having user registration/account creation.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Personalizing a sponsorship page can be implemented as a standalone feature for sponsors (page existence can be part of this feature).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Listing summits with their dates/times depends on summit basic information (including schedule/time) being defined.

evaluations.rationale: This explicitly depends on a multi-page registration process existing.

evaluations.evidence: find a link in the menu that links to the registration form
evaluations.rationale: A menu link to the registration form depends on the registration form existing.

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: User registration can be implemented as a standalone foundational feature without requiring another story first.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Finding session information can be implemented as a standalone browsing/search feature (it does not inherently require a specific other story to be implemented first).
